about: Every semantic rule of the det-port Java runtime (gitgalaxy/tools/cobol_to_java/det/cobolrt, #4711): a stable ID, the IBM reference it implements, the options it depends on (#4704), its oracle-assumptions register entries (docs/language_status/register/) and its calibration (#4702). Each rule's code site carries `[rule ID]`; tests/cobol_mainframe/test_cobolrt_rules.py checks both directions.

Status, against IBM (the reference; GnuCOBOL is the instrument): MATCHED -- the runtime implements IBM's documented rule; DIFFERS -- it follows the oracle where z/OS differs or where IBM documents no result and the oracle's answer is modelled (declared in the register); ASSUMED -- IBM leaves it open or the runtime's reading of IBM is not yet confirmed, the choice named; REFUSED -- the runtime stops by name. Calibration: uncalibrated until a z/OS measurement backs the rule (#4702).

rules.title: TRUNC(STD / BIN / OPT) set for one program's run and restored after it (a program LINKed or CALLed keeps its own)
ARITH(EXTEND) set for one program's run and restored after it
NUMPROC(PFD / NOPFD) set for one program's run and restored after it (NUMPROC(MIG) compiles as NOPFD)
A zero divisor raises the size error and makes the intermediate libcob's NaN: NaN in, NaN out through + - * and unary minus, and a store of NaN leaves the receiver unchanged
An intermediate quotient as cob_decimal_div forms it: scale a.scale - b.scale, the dividend shifted 38 digits more, truncated (38 + max(scale, 0) decimal places)
DIVIDE ... REMAINDER: dividend less divisor times the quotient truncated to the first GIVING receiver's scale (not to its high-order digits); a NaN quotient leaves the remainder receiver unchanged
A division inside an intrinsic function's argument (cob_intr_binop): a zero divisor gives 0 with the size error raised, never NaN
rules.ibm_note: z/OS leaves a zero divisor's result undefined; the oracle's value is modelled

rules.title: ARITHMETIC-OSVS: an intermediate truncated to the statement's decimal places as cob_decimal_align does it (fewer places than the scale lose as many low-order digits: 579 aligned to 2 places is 500)
rules.ibm_note: OS/VS COBOL arithmetic is outside the Enterprise COBOL manuals; cobc's arithmetic-osvs (the oracle) is modelled

rules.title: A numeric literal in a decimal expression is libcob's decimal constant: an ADD / SUBTRACT raises its scale and an exponent trims it in place, and later uses of the same literal see the change; a program restart resets it
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents literal operands as constants; the in-place scale change is the oracle's (cob_decimal_* on dc_N)

rules.title: a ** b as cob_decimal_pow: a whole exponent exactly, else through double; 0 ** 0 is 1 with the size error raised, a non-finite result NaN with the size error raised

ibm.section: SIZE ERROR phrases (Table 32: exponentiation size errors)

rules.title: A MOVE between zoned items of one shape (digits, scale, sign, sign position, size) copies the bytes: a non-digit travels as it is, no sign rewrite
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric item; the oracle's (GnuCOBOL 3.1.2) rule is modelled (cobc compiles the MOVE as a memcpy)

rules.title: MOVE by receiver category: alphanumeric padded / truncated (JUSTIFIED on the right), alphanumeric-edited through its insertion characters, numeric aligned on the decimal point with extra decimals and high-order digits dropped, numeric-edited through its PICTURE (BLANK WHEN ZERO), a group as bytes

A zoned sender holding a non-digit MOVEd to a binary item: each byte counts as its character minus '0', accumulated in an unsigned 64-bit integer (wrapping), the receiver's digits kept under TRUNC(STD)
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric item; the oracle's (GnuCOBOL 3.1.2) rule is modelled (cob_move_display_to_binary)

rules.title: A signed zoned sender whose sign byte is neither a digit, an overpunch, a sign nor a space, MOVEd to a binary item (a separate sign) or to an alphanumeric item: refused by name
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for such data

rules.title: A zoned sender holding a non-digit MOVEd to a zoned, packed or numeric-edited receiver: the oracle's byte rules (Zoned)
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric item; the oracle's (GnuCOBOL 3.1.2) rule is modelled

rules.title: A MOVE with a COMP-1 / COMP-2 sender or receiver: a number into a float converted to its precision, a float into a fixed-point or edited item rounded in the low-order position (9 / 18 significant digits); a float's bytes moved otherwise refused
X'hh..' is exactly those bytes, with no code-page translation; the record charset keeps every byte value

MOVE of a figurative constant: ZERO stored as the value zero (numeric, edited), SPACE / LOW-VALUE / HIGH-VALUE / QUOTE as their byte repeated; a figurative other than ZERO into a COMP-1 / COMP-2 item refused
MOVE ALL literal: the literal repeated to the receiver's size
A numeric sender MOVEd to an alphanumeric receiver as its unsigned digits (the overpunched sign removed); a right-P item's P positions as zeros
A numeric-edited sender MOVEd to a numeric receiver is de-edited: its digits, negative when it shows -, CR or DB

An alphanumeric sender MOVEd to a numeric receiver read as libcob does: into a zoned item byte for byte (leading spaces and one sign skipped, a stray character makes it zero), into a packed or binary item the whole text
A numeric item's value as an operand (numeric-edited: de-edited; a zoned item through Zoned's reading)
The operand of ADD / SUBTRACT that cobc compiles as cob_add_int(y, cob_get_int(x)): a zoned x of at most 9 digits read as an int, a non-digit as its byte minus '0'
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric item; the oracle's (GnuCOBOL 3.1.2) rule is modelled

rules.title: The receiver of ADD / SUBTRACT / MULTIPLY / DIVIDE, the PERFORM VARYING variable and the SET UP / DOWN BY target are read before it stores: a zoned receiver holding a non-digit is refused by name
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result (ZONEDATA(PFD) assumes valid zone bits; ZONEDATA(NOPFD|MIG) corrects them on an addition)

rules.title: A STRING / UNSTRING POINTER, an UNSTRING TALLYING IN item and an INSPECT TALLYING counter are read before they store: a zoned one holding a non-digit is refused by name
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result (ZONEDATA(PFD) assumes valid zone bits); the same ground as the receiver of ADD

rules.title: A numeric item's value in a comparison: a zoned item holding a non-digit as the oracle compares it (Zoned.compareValue)
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric item; the oracle's (GnuCOBOL 3.1.2) rule is modelled

rules.title: An alphanumeric item's text: its bytes; a value moved into it truncated on the right or padded with spaces

An arithmetic result stored: low-order digits past the scale dropped or ROUNDED (half away from zero), high-order digits past the PICTURE (or the bytes, TRUNC(BIN) / COMP-5) lost; the typed-layer readers return exactly what the store leaves
ADD / SUBTRACT into an unsigned binary item where cobc compiles native arithmetic: the receiver takes the absolute value (1 - 3 is 2), as IBM; the oracle wraps (declared)

ibm.section: MOVE statement: elementary moves; SIZE ERROR phrases

rules.title: ON SIZE ERROR: the receiver unchanged, and the condition true, when the value does not fit or is NaN
A Db2 value into a binary host variable takes any value its 2 / 4 / 8 bytes hold whatever TRUNC says (SMALLINT / INTEGER / BIGINT); -304 only outside that type

ibm.section: Equivalent SQL and COBOL data types

rules.title: Nonnumeric operands compared byte by byte, the shorter padded with spaces, in the data's byte order or under the PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE's alphabet (ASCII data on the oracle, EBCDIC on z/OS)
A numeric item against a nonnumeric one is its digits as characters (as if moved to an alphanumeric item of as many characters), the sign dropped
Numeric operands compared by value, whatever their usage and the collating sequence
A comparison with a floating-point comparand is made in floating point: a fixed-point item converted to long HFP
An item against an ALL literal: the literal repeated or cut to the item's length, then compared byte by byte
An item against a figurative constant: the constant's character repeated to the item's length (ZERO against a numeric item: by value)

IS NUMERIC: zoned digits with a valid overpunch at the sign position, packed digit nibbles with a valid sign nibble, alphanumeric all digits; under NUMPROC(PFD) a signed item with an F sign is refused
IS ALPHABETIC / ALPHABETIC-UPPER / ALPHABETIC-LOWER: letters and spaces only
DISPLAY of an operand: a signed zoned item as its bytes, a binary or packed item as zoned digits of its PICTURE (signed: the last digit overpunched), any other item as its bytes
STRING ... DELIMITED BY ... INTO ... [WITH POINTER]: bytes transferred in order, the receiver not padded; OVERFLOW when the pointer is outside the receiver or the data does not fit

UNSTRING ... DELIMITED BY ... INTO ... [DELIMITER IN] [COUNT IN] [WITH POINTER] [TALLYING]: the rest to the first INTO with no delimiter; OVERFLOW when the pointer is outside the source or characters remain
INSPECT TALLYING / REPLACING / CONVERTING with BEFORE / AFTER: the phrases act on the original text, the earlier clause takes the characters, TALLYING and REPLACING are separate passes
A LINK's COMMAREA is the caller's storage from the area's first byte, up to the end of the caller's record; bytes past it are LOW-VALUES here (z/OS shows whatever storage follows)
INITIALIZE REPLACING of a table leaves the categories it does not name as they are (IBM); the port stops by name when the occurrences differ, because the oracle copies the first over the others
A COMP / COMP-4 / BINARY item under TRUNC(STD) holds at most its PICTURE's digits (high-order ones lost); under TRUNC(BIN), and a COMP-5 item always, whatever its 2 / 4 / 8 bytes hold
TRUNC(OPT): results as TRUNC(STD), and a value stored past a binary receiver's PICTURE stops by name (IBM: the result is unpredictable)
ARITH(EXTEND): an intermediate result past 30 digits stops by name (GnuCOBOL caps none; IBM's EXTEND range is not modelled)
NUMPROC(PFD): a zoned or packed value read with a sign that is not preferred (C / D signed, F unsigned) is refused by name

ibm.section: Sign representation of zoned and packed-decimal data

rules.title: A zoned item's sign overpunched on its last (or first) digit: + as { A-I, - as } J-R (the ASCII form of the C / D zones); written with the preferred sign; SIGN SEPARATE as + / -

ibm.section: Sign representation of zoned and packed-decimal data

rules.title: A packed item: two digits a byte, the last nibble the sign (D and B negative), written C / D signed and F unsigned

ibm.section: Sign representation of zoned and packed-decimal data

rules.title: A COMP / COMP-4 / BINARY item is big-endian two's complement; a COMP-5 item is in the oracle's native (little-endian) order, z/OS's being big-endian
Whether a value fits its receiver without losing high-order digits: the PICTURE's digits, or the bytes' range for a binary item under TRUNC(BIN) and COMP-5 (the size error test)
libcob's GET_SIGN / PUT_SIGN on a signed zoned item: the sign byte read as a digit and a sign, and written back as an overpunch after a MOVE from it or an arithmetic read
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric item; the oracle's (GnuCOBOL 3.1.2) rule is modelled

rules.title: A zoned operand holding a non-digit (cob_decimal_set_display, cob_get_int): HIGH- / LOW-VALUES first byte as +/-10^size, leading zero-nibble bytes skipped, the rest accumulated as byte - '0' in a wrapping unsigned 64-bit (or 32-bit) integer
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric item; the oracle's (GnuCOBOL 3.1.2) rule is modelled

rules.title: A zoned comparand holding a non-digit (cob_cmp_numdisp): every digit position counts in a signed 64-bit integer, a sign byte that is no overpunch 0, nothing written back
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric item; the oracle's (GnuCOBOL 3.1.2) rule is modelled

rules.title: A zoned sender holding a non-digit MOVEd to a zoned (bytes aligned, space or X'00' as '0'), numeric-edited (bytes as the PICTURE's digits) or packed item ((hi * 16 + lo) mod 256)
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric item; the oracle's (GnuCOBOL 3.1.2) rule is modelled

rules.title: Refused by name: a non-digit in a P-scaled item read as an operand or comparand, in an arithmetic receiver, or across 19 or more digits
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for non-digit data, and the oracle's results there follow no rule

rules.title: COMP-1 / COMP-2 are HFP: sign bit, excess-64 characteristic (a power of 16), 6 / 14 hexadecimal fraction digits, big-endian; true zero all zero bytes; an unnormalized fraction reads as its value
An exponent overflow (past 16**63) or underflow (below 16**-65) is refused by name: z/OS's answer depends on the program mask and Language Environment
ADD / SUBTRACT: the operands aligned with one hexadecimal guard digit, the sum normalized and truncated
MULTIPLY: the exact product truncated to the precision
DIVIDE: the exact quotient truncated to the precision
A zero divisor: as a statement's whole value, libcob's NaN with the size error raised (the receiver unchanged); inside a larger expression refused by name
rules.ibm_note: z/OS leaves a zero divisor's result undefined; the oracle's NaN is modelled

rules.title: A long value into a COMP-1 is rounded (LOAD ROUNDED: a one added at the first discarded bit)
An IEEE binary32 / binary64 pattern to and from COMP-1 / COMP-2: binary64 exact in long HFP, binary32 truncated to long then rounded to short, HFP to IEEE nearest ties to even
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no IEEE converter for COMP-1 / COMP-2; the model's choice (det/hfp.py from_ieee / to_ieee)

rules.title: A fixed-point value converted to long HFP: the exact value truncated to 14 hexadecimal digits (then rounded to short for a COMP-1)
rules.ibm_note: IBM does not document the generated conversion; truncation is the model's choice

rules.title: A floating-point exponentiation: the exact power for an integer exponent, exp(b ln a) at 60 digits for a fractional one, truncated to long HFP
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for a floating-point exponentiation; the capture kit's reference power() is the model until captured z/OS output agrees

rules.title: A float moved to a fixed-point item: rounded in the receiver's low-order position, at most 9 (COMP-1) / 18 (COMP-2) significant digits
FUNCTION NUMVAL / NUMVAL-C in a floating-point expression: long HFP of the value under ARITH(COMPAT); more than 18 digits, or more than 15 significant ones, refused by name
A statement that is floating point only through NUMVAL stores its result into a fixed-point receiver rounded half away from zero, as a float MOVE is
DISPLAY of a COMP-1 / COMP-2 item as -.9(8)E-99 / -.9(17)E-99, the mantissa rounded half away from zero
A number through a numeric-edited PICTURE: 9, Z / * zero suppression, the . and , insertion characters, fixed + / -, CR / DB, B 0 /, and a zero value of an all-suppression PICTURE
A floating insertion string ($$$,$$9.99, +++9, ---9) floats the sign or currency string to just left of the first significant digit; every digit position in the string and a zero value: all spaces
The currency symbol ($ or the declared PICTURE SYMBOL) stands for the program's CURRENCY SIGN string
A zoned sender holding non-digits: its bytes are the PICTURE's digits as they are, only a '0' suppressed
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric item; the oracle's (GnuCOBOL 3.1.2) rule is modelled (cob_move_display_to_edited)

rules.title: An edit PICTURE's integer and decimal digit positions (floating insertion included); under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA the , is its decimal point
FUNCTION UPPER-CASE / LOWER-CASE of single-byte letters
FUNCTION REVERSE
FUNCTION TRIM [LEADING / TRAILING]: spaces only removed (low-values stay); an all-space argument gives a zero-length result, as the oracle
FUNCTION MOD (a - b * FLOOR(a / b)) and REM (a - b * INTEGER-PART(a / b)); a zero b gives 0 with no size error, as the oracle
FUNCTION INTEGER (floor), INTEGER-PART (toward zero), ABS, MIN, MAX

ibm.section: Intrinsic functions: INTEGER, INTEGER-PART, ABS, MIN, MAX

rules.title: FUNCTION NUMVAL / NUMVAL-C: the number in a text (spaces, one sign + - CR DB, a decimal point; NUMVAL-C a currency sign and commas)
FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL / TEST-NUMVAL-C: 0 when valid, else the position of the first character that makes it invalid (the length + 1 when it ends early), as the oracle
FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE where the project has no clock bean: YYYYMMDDHHMMSShh and the UTC offset of the run's clock
FUNCTION RANDOM: one run unit's sequence (glibc random_r TYPE_3, as the oracle); the numbers differ from z/OS's, the interface as IBM documents it
FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE / DATE-OF-INTEGER: day 1 is 1 January 1601 (INTDATE(ANSI)) or 15 October 1582 (INTDATE(LILIAN))
ACCEPT FROM DATE / DATE YYYYMMDD / DAY / DAY YYYYDDD / TIME: the run's clock as the unsigned integer item IBM describes, moved as that item

ibm.section: ACCEPT statement: Format 2 (system date and time)

rules.title: ACCEPT identifier FROM SYSIN: the next line of standard input moved to the target as an alphanumeric MOVE; no record left stops the run by name
rules.ibm_note: IBM leaves the target undefined when the input stream is exhausted; the port refuses by name instead of blanking it

rules.title: A POINTER in a COMMAREA DTO: NULL as all zero bytes; an address, which names storage the port does not have, stops the run by name
rules.ibm_note: an address is not portable between the two sides

rules.title: A keyed file's records in key order: READ by full key the first record whose key equals it; the keys ordered as the file is
READ GTEQ / GENERIC: in key order, the first record whose key's first LENGTH bytes equal the given ones, or with GTEQ are greater
A command's FROM(area) LENGTH(n): n bytes from the area's first byte, which may run past the area into what follows it in its record
A WRITEQ TS / TD whose LENGTH runs past its FROM item writes FROM's bytes then spaces to LENGTH (ASSUMED: IBM takes the storage that follows, undefined)
DOCUMENT CREATE TEXT / BINARY LENGTH(n): n bytes of the area (negative: LENGERR); DOCUMENT RETRIEVE INTO: at most MAXLENGTH bytes, the rest of INTO as it was; past the area refused
SEND TEXT FROM(f) LENGTH(n) past FROM sends the items that follow it in its record; past the record's end refused

XCTL COMMAREA(area) LENGTH(n) past the target's DFHCOMMAREA: n bytes travel (EIBCALEN = n), the ones the DTO cannot carry as the region's EBCDIC bytes; another program's DTO as its layout's bytes, a class with no layout refused
PUT CONTAINER FROM FLENGTH(n): the first n bytes (negative: LENGERR RESP2 1); GET CONTAINER INTO FLENGTH: the most the area takes; a FLENGTH past the area refused
START FROM(f) LENGTH(n): the first n bytes, LENGERR when LENGTH is not greater than zero; past FROM refused
RETRIEVE RTRANSID / RTERMID / QUEUE: the value MOVEd into the program's area, padded with spaces or truncated; RETRIEVE INTO the bytes
READ INTO LENGTH(max): the record truncated to max, LENGERR (RESP2 11) when longer, the rest of INTO as it was; a negative LENGTH or a record past INTO refused
READQ TD INTO: the record (cut to LENGTH) goes INTO, the rest of INTO as it was; a record moved past INTO refused
BIF DEEDIT: the characters other than the digits removed, the digits right-aligned and zero-padded, a trailing sign kept as the last digit's zone
TS items are in the region's code page (the estate's EBCDIC page, else CCSID 037): the program's bytes moved byte for byte, a byte with no character in both pages stops the run by name
rules.ibm_note: the region's code page is a deployment fact IBM leaves to the installation

rules.title: ASSIGN of a short value (SYSID: 4 bytes) into a longer area: the first bytes, the rest as it was
A symbolic map field's subfields: attribute, colour and highlight bytes (X'00' and a space not set), length -1 the cursor; RECEIVE MAP's input text padded and its length without trailing blanks
RECEIVE MAP into a DFHMDF JUSTIFY=(LEFT|RIGHT[,BLANK|ZERO]) field: the typed text placed at the justified end, the rest filled with blanks or zeros; <f>L the length typed
FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE in a CICS task: the task's clock, the region's zone (UTC)
The RESP value of each condition, and the condition of each value (DFHRESP)
A condition with no HANDLE CONDITION label abends, except those IBM's default action ignores (EOC)
HANDLE AID: the label of the key pressed, else ANYKEY's (not ENTER); none: the next statement; PUSH / POP HANDLE save and restore the state
RECEIVE INTO: the data into the first bytes of the area, the rest as it was; RECEIVE SET: the data copied into the record, a byte past it X'00'
GETMAIN SET (INITIMG, LENGERR RESP2 1 sets the pointer to zero), WEB RECEIVE SET, SET ADDRESS OF / SET pointer TO ADDRESS OF: handles to blocks of task storage, a record and its block one storage
ADDRESS COMMAREA(ptr): the handle of the DFHCOMMAREA record's bytes; a task with no COMMAREA is refused (IBM's X'FF000000' is no COBOL NULL)
SET(ptr) of RECEIVE, RETRIEVE, READQ TS, GET CONTAINER, READ, READNEXT and READPREV: a new block of task storage holding the data, its handle in the pointer, valid until the command IBM names ends it

OS/VS COBOL chained storage areas: an address moved between a BLL cell and a fullword of data is a token both runtimes number alike (0 NULL, the n-th address n * 65536; a value no cell gave is refused), and a record is addressed again through its cell at a paragraph name (a null cell leaves it as it is)
rules.ibm_note: CICS/MVS 2.1.2 Application Programmer's Reference SC33-0512-1, 'BLL and chained storage areas' (p. 22): not an online IBM doc; the token is assumed (a real address does not fit a fullword in the instrument)

rules.title: A planned SQL fault (PROGRAM LINE NTH SQLCODE SQLSTATE) replaces the statement's execution, the SQLCA set as Db2 would set it
rules.ibm_note: the faults are the harness's; the SQLCA a fault leaves is assumed

rules.title: The SQLCA a statement leaves: SQLCODE 0 and no warning before its outcome, then Db2's SQLCODE, SQLSTATE, SQLERRM tokens, SQLERRP, SQLERRD and warnings (IBM's driver's own SQLCA where it has one)
Host variables in: PIC X(n) as CHAR(n) (trailing blanks kept), a 49-level pair as VARCHAR, a numeric item as DECIMAL / SMALLINT / INTEGER / BIGINT, NULL when the indicator is negative

ibm.section: Equivalent SQL and COBOL data types

rules.title: A searched UPDATE / DELETE (or INSERT ... SELECT) that changes no row is SQLCODE +100
SELECT INTO: the one row; no row +100, more than one -811

A row into host variables: a string padded or truncated (SQLWARN0 / SQLWARN1 'W', the indicator the original length), a number whose integer part does not fit -304 and nothing assigned, NULL without an indicator -305
COMMIT: the unit of work committed, cursors not WITH HOLD closed; ROLLBACK: backed out, every cursor closed; refused with no unit of work
SAVEPOINT / ROLLBACK TO / RELEASE SAVEPOINT as written, on the unit's connection (-880: no such savepoint), set ON ROLLBACK RETAIN CURSORS
OPEN (-502 when open; WITH HOLD survives COMMIT), FETCH (+100 at the end, -501 when not open), CLOSE (-501 when not open); a task's or step's end closes its cursors
UPDATE / DELETE WHERE CURRENT OF: the current row (-501 not open, -508 no current row)
The 12-byte feedback code: all zero for success, else severity 3, the message number, case / severity / control and 'CEE'; what the model does not model refused by name
Lilian day 1 is 15 October 1582 (Gregorian leap years); Lilian second 86400 is 00:00:00 on that day; a seconds item travels by value in its own usage (COMP-2: HFP on z/OS)
Picture strings: the date / time terms LE documents, formatted and parsed; any other term refused by name

ibm.section: Picture character terms and picture strings

rules.title: A VSTRING result: halfword length then the text, the rest of the item untouched
CEEGMT / CEEUTC: the run's clock is GMT; Lilian day and seconds

ibm.section: CEEGMT: get current Greenwich Mean Time

rules.title: CEEGMTO / CEEUTCO: the offset from GMT is zero on the GMT clock

ibm.section: CEEGMTO: get offset from Greenwich Mean Time to local time

rules.title: COBDATFT (CardDemo's assembler date routine): input type '2' to output type '2' modelled byte for byte; type '1' and the error path depend on the load module's literal pool: refused
MVSWAIT (CardDemo's assembler wait routine): returns at once with RETURN-CODE 0, caller storage untouched (the timer wait is not observable); an argument shorter than the fullword it loads: refused
ENTRY 'DLITCBL': each DB PCB of the PSB bound to the area IMS passes, its mask filled (DBD name, level 00, blank status, PROCOPT, sensitive segments, key feedback zero)

The stated database: DBD / PSB configuration and seed loaded in hierarchic sequence (refused when out of order), new twins placed by segment type and sequence field, each database written at the step's end

SSAs: segment name, unqualified (blank) or qualified (field, relational operator, value, ')'); qualification statements joined by AND (& or *) and OR (+ or |), AND binding tighter, at most 16; AC / AJ / AK as IBM answers them; command codes F, L, P, C, D and - (L only on the last unqualified SSA of a GU, P only on a GU, C only as the one SSA of a GU, D on a get call), the other codes, the independent AND (#) and missing levels refused
A qualification compares the field's stored bytes (C / X); a P field only where packed and logical comparison agree (both valid, one positive sign)
The PCB mask after a call: status code, segment level, segment name, concatenated key and its length

GU / GN / GNP and their holds: the first segment in hierarchic sequence satisfying the SSAs, from the database's start, from position, or under parentage; GE / GB / GP / GA / GK; position and parentage after the call; command code D hands back the D-coded segments before the found one

ibm.section: GU / GHU, GN / GHN, GNP / GHNP calls

rules.title: EXEC DLI GU / GN / GNP USING PCB(n) [SEGMENT WHERE] INTO under CICS: the CBLTDLI get of the same SSAs against PCB n of the scheduled PSB, a hold where PROCOPT allows an update; DIBSTAT the PCB's status
rules.ibm_note: EXEC DLI has no HOLD option; the hold on an updating PROCOPT is assumed (register I5)

rules.title: EXEC DLI ISRT USING PCB(n) SEGMENT(s) [WHERE ...] ... SEGMENT(t) FROM(area) [SEGLENGTH(n)] under CICS: the CBLTDLI ISRT of the same SSAs against PCB n of the scheduled PSB; segments are fixed length, so a SEGLENGTH that differs from the DBD's stops the run; DIBSTAT the PCB's status
rules.ibm_note: Segments are fixed length (the DBD's); a variable-length SEGLENGTH is refused by name (register I5)

rules.title: EXEC DLI REPL / DLET USING PCB(n) SEGMENT(s) FROM(area) under CICS: the CBLTDLI REPL / DLET of the segment the previous get on this PCB held (DJ with none, DA for a changed key); SEGMENT must name the held segment's type; DIBSTAT the PCB's status
rules.ibm_note: The command form has no SSA, so SEGMENT is checked against the held segment's type; the hold comes from the get-hold on an updating PROCOPT (register I5)

rules.title: ISRT: the segment under the parent its SSAs (or current position) locate, among its twins by sequence field; II for a key its twins hold, GE for a parent not found; with command code D, a path insert from the root (each D-coded level kept or created from its slice of the I/O area); on a load-mode PCB (PROCOPT L / LS) the segment is appended in sequence, LB / LC / LD / LE for a duplicate, out-of-sequence, parentless or type-order violation
REPL / DLET on the segment the previous get-hold call returned; DJ without one, DA when the I/O area changed the sequence field; DLET removes the segment's dependents

CALL 'CBLTDLI' USING function pcb io-area [ssa ...]: the PCB the program was passed, the function's dispatch (AD for an unknown function, AM for one PROCOPT does not allow), any other DL/I call refused

A GSAM PCB in load mode: ISRT appends one record of the DBD's length to the output file, any other function is AM, and the PCB mask's segment level is blank; an SSA or an I/O area shorter than the record is refused

EXEC DLI SCHD PSB under CICS: the databases load at the first SCHD, the PSB's PCBs start with no position, DIBSTAT blank; a PSB already scheduled is TC (with NODHABEND), else refused; a planned TC (#5233) schedules the PSB first
EXEC DLI TERM: the scheduled PSB is released (the databases keep what was written), DIBSTAT blank; a TERM with no PSB scheduled is refused
A planned DL/I fault (# DLI FUNCTION NTH|* STATUS; a get-hold counts as its get) replaces that call's execution, the PCB answering the status as for any status it names
rules.ibm_note: the faults are the harness's; the PCB feedback a fault leaves is assumed

rules.title: A COMP / COMP-4 / BINARY / COMP-5 item of 1-4 digits is a halfword, 5-9 a fullword, 10-18 a doubleword
A subscript is 1-based: offset + (index - 1) * the entry's length
Reference modification (start 1-based, no length: to the end) is an alphanumeric view of the item's bytes
A storage area (WORKING-STORAGE, LINKAGE, an FD record, a map) is its bytes; a DFHCOMMAREA of a stated EIBCALEN holds only those bytes, so a reference past them fails
Every byte value survives the record charset (a single-byte charset made lossless); X'hh..' is exactly its bytes
An ALPHABET (EBCDIC, or literals with ALSO and THRU): each data byte's position, the bytes no entry names after them in native order
A relation condition's nonnumeric operands under PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE: the shorter padded with spaces, then position by position in the alphabet
A key comparison IBM's EBCDIC sequence and the oracle's byte order decide differently, or one over a byte with no EBCDIC character, stops the run by name
SORT / MERGE keys compare as their items do in a relation condition (numeric by value, others byte by byte), the first the major key, ASCENDING / DESCENDING each
Equal keys come out in the order they went in (WITH DUPLICATES IN ORDER; the model keeps it always); MERGE: equal keys in the order the files are named
RELEASE / RETURN only inside the input / output procedure, USING files' records as they are, GIVING files each receiving every record; an implicit OPEN / READ / CLOSE that fails stops by name
OPEN / CLOSE / READ / WRITE / REWRITE through CobolFiles, returning the FILE STATUS (the harness's planned statuses apply)
A keyed READ / WRITE / REWRITE: the record whose key bytes equal the record area's, found by the repository and verified against the key bytes
A keyed file with no store bound: OPEN and CLOSE (their statuses) only; a record operation is a hole
rules.ibm_note: a record operation the translator could not bind is not modelled

rules.title: DISPLAY [WITH NO ADVANCING] to SYSOUT: the operands joined, in the record charset (a byte the charset leaves unmapped as its latin-1 byte), a record per DISPLAY
A user abend (CEE3ABD) carries its code, U followed by four digits

ibm.section: CEE3ABD: terminate enclave with an abend

rules.title: The task's queue manager: local queues, CCSID and messages from the case's mq.cfg; a name it does not hold is MQRC_UNKNOWN_OBJECT_NAME
rules.ibm_note: the queues are the case's facts, not a z/OS queue manager's

rules.title: Only a CICS MQI call with Hconn MQHC_DEF_HCONN (0) is modelled; any other Hconn or MQI verb is refused by name
rules.ibm_note: the runtime stops by name outside the modelled calls

rules.title: MQOPEN: resolves the object descriptor, makes the object handle (1, 2, 3 ... in the order opened)
rules.ibm_note: the handle value is opaque in IBM's; the runtime's numbering is the oracle's

rules.title: MQCLOSE: the handle becomes MQHO_UNUSABLE_HOBJ (-1)
rules.ibm_note: IBM documents the handle's reset; the options handled are those the model gives meaning to

rules.title: MQGET (destructive): highest priority first, first in first out within it; WAIT on an empty queue ends at once with 2033, MQWI_UNLIMITED refused; MQGMO_CONVERT a no-op where the message is as asked, refused otherwise
rules.ibm_note: no concurrent producer is assumed; conversion beyond the identity is refused

rules.title: MQPUT / MQPUT1: MsgId GGMQ + a counter, the put context (PutApplType, PutDate / PutTime from the pinned clock, identity placeholders), the message queued under the unit of work
rules.ibm_note: the MsgId form and identity-context placeholders are the oracle's

rules.title: The MQ unit of work is the CICS task's: SYNCPOINT commits, SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK and an abend back out (BackoutCount raised), the task's end commits
rules.ibm_note: IBM's rule is modelled; the oracle's joint syncpoint with ggcics.c is assumed

rules.title: SET ADDRESS OF a record TO a pointer into the PSA (a NULL pointer is address 0), the TCB (PSATNEW) or the TIOT (TCBTIO), and the pointer moved along its block through a numeric item it REDEFINES: the blocks laid from the stated job step at IBM's offsets; a record or an advance past what is laid is refused
